Notes: One of two pictorial scales in the same deposit; the enjoyment scale is morano_2019_enjoyment. The deposit has no respondent identifier, so id is row position.

Description: Pictorial physical activity enjoyment scale, 4 items on a 1-5 scale, Italian schoolchildren. 56,140 responses from 14,035 respondents on 4 items.
Reference: Morano M, Bortoli L, Ruiz MC, Vitali F, Robazza C (2019). Self-efficacy and enjoyment of physical activity in children: factorial validity of two pictorial scales. PeerJ, 7, e7402. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.7402
Notes: Companion to morano_2019_self_efficacy from the same deposit. The deposit has no respondent identifier, so id is row position.

Description: School self-efficacy scale, 12 items on a 1-5 scale, Italian schoolchildren, with motor-fitness covariates (6-minute walk, standing broad jump, 4x10 shuttle) and BMI class. 47,544 responses from 3,962 respondents on 12 items.
Reference: Codella R, Puci MV, Vandoni M, Correale L, Galvani C, Togni F, Casolo F, Passi A, Orizio C, Alberti G, Esposito F, Montomoli C, La Torre A (2020). School self-efficacy is affected by gender and motor skills: findings from an Italian study. PeerJ, 8, e8949. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.8949
Notes: The deposited .xls has a banner in row 0, so the header is row 1; read with header=0 the item block is invisible. Items are numbered item_1..item_12 in source order because the English column headers are full sentences.

Description: Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale-Short Form (IUS-12), Chinese version, 12 items on a 1-5 scale. 18,612 responses from 1,551 respondents on 12 items.
Reference: Ding X, Zhao Z, Wang J, Chen C, Ding S, Gao J, Deng J, Liu D (2025). Relationships between different components of intolerance of uncertainty and symptoms of obsessive-compulsive disorder: a network analysis. PeerJ, 13, e19791. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.19791
Notes: The deposited .tsv has no header row -- its first line is a respondent. Columns 0-1 are gender and age; 2-13 are the IU items and 14-31 the OCI-R items (ding_2025_ocd). Block numbering follows the paper's own node labels (IU6, OCD3). No respondent identifier in the deposit, so id is row position.

Description: Obsessive-Compulsive Inventory-Revised (OCI-R), Chinese version, 18 items on a 1-5 scale. 27,918 responses from 1,551 respondents on 18 items.
Reference: Ding X, Zhao Z, Wang J, Chen C, Ding S, Gao J, Deng J, Liu D (2025). Relationships between different components of intolerance of uncertainty and symptoms of obsessive-compulsive disorder: a network analysis. PeerJ, 13, e19791. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.19791
Notes: Companion to ding_2025_iu from the same headerless .tsv; see that table's note for the column layout.

Description: Zimbardo Time Perspective Inventory, 20 items on a 1-5 scale, Chinese college students. 10,520 responses from 526 respondents on 20 items.
Reference: Pan W, Ma Y, Long Y, Wang Y, Zhao Y (2023). Self-control mediates the relationship between time perspective and mobile phone addiction in Chinese college students. PeerJ, 11, e16467. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.16467
Notes: The deposit labels its three item blocks only a*/b*/c*. This block is the ZTPI: the authors' subscale columns for it are PP, PN, PH, PF and F. Items keep the source's a1..a20 numbering; no published item numbering is asserted.

Description: Mobile Phone Addiction Tendency Scale (MPATS), 16 items on a 1-5 scale, Chinese college students. 8,416 responses from 526 respondents on 16 items.
Reference: Pan W, Ma Y, Long Y, Wang Y, Zhao Y (2023). Self-control mediates the relationship between time perspective and mobile phone addiction in Chinese college students. PeerJ, 11, e16467. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.16467
Notes: The b* block of the deposit, identified by the authors' ATP/HH/AE/RT subscale columns and by matching MPATS's published 16-item length. `b8` appears twice in the header; positionally the second is b9 and is restored as such.

Description: Self-Control Scale, 19 items on a 1-5 scale, Chinese college students. 9,994 responses from 526 respondents on 19 items.
Reference: Pan W, Ma Y, Long Y, Wang Y, Zhao Y (2023). Self-control mediates the relationship between time perspective and mobile phone addiction in Chinese college students. PeerJ, 11, e16467. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.16467
Notes: The c* block of the deposit. Identified by the authors' WS/S/SC/MC/IC subscales and by their `Self-control total` running 29-91, inside the 19-95 a 19-item 1-5 scale allows.

Description: Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale (DERS), 36 items on a 1-5 scale, Israeli community sample. 8,385 responses from 233 respondents on 36 items.
Reference: Lev-Ari L, Zohar AH, Bachner-Melman R (2021). Eating for numbing: a community-based study of trauma exposure, emotion dysregulation, dissociation, body dissatisfaction and eating disorder symptoms. PeerJ, 9, e11899. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.11899
Notes: id does NOT link people across waves. The deposit has a two-valued `time` column carried here as `wave`, and its `code` column cannot serve as a participant id -- null for 5 rows, literally 0 for 70 more, and 75 (code, time) pairs duplicated. A person present at both waves therefore appears as two unlinked ids.

Description: Eating Disorder Examination Questionnaire (EDE-Q), 22 items on a 0-6 scale, Israeli community sample. 5,126 responses from 233 respondents on 22 items.
Reference: Lev-Ari L, Zohar AH, Bachner-Melman R (2021). Eating for numbing: a community-based study of trauma exposure, emotion dysregulation, dissociation, body dissatisfaction and eating disorder symptoms. PeerJ, 9, e11899. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.11899
Notes: Same deposit and the same wave caveat as lev_ari_2021_ders: id does not link people across the two waves.

Description: Dissociative Experiences Scale (DES), 14 items on a 1-11 scale, Israeli community sample. 3,261 responses from 233 respondents on 14 items.
Reference: Lev-Ari L, Zohar AH, Bachner-Melman R (2021). Eating for numbing: a community-based study of trauma exposure, emotion dysregulation, dissociation, body dissatisfaction and eating disorder symptoms. PeerJ, 9, e11899. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.11899
Notes: Same deposit and the same wave caveat as lev_ari_2021_ders: id does not link people across the two waves.

Description: PHQ-9 depression screen, 9 items on a 0-3 scale, Chinese nurses. 2,637 responses from 293 respondents on 9 items.
Reference: Qi X, Xu HN (2024). The impact of nurses' stress situation coping on somatization: a mediated moderation model. PeerJ, 12, e18658. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.18658
Notes: One of five instruments in one deposited sheet; the authors' `* Total score` columns are composites and are excluded.

Description: Somatic symptom scale, 15 items on a 1-4 scale, Chinese nurses. 4,395 responses from 293 respondents on 15 items.
Reference: Qi X, Xu HN (2024). The impact of nurses' stress situation coping on somatization: a mediated moderation model. PeerJ, 12, e18658. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.18658
Notes: Five columns inside this block carry PHQ/GAD names (PHQ3, PHQ4, PHQ1, GAD1, PHQ7 repeated) while holding this block's 1-4 scale. SSS1..SSS15 are complete without them, so those five are excluded rather than guessed at.

Description: Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10), 10 items on a 0-4 scale, Chinese nurses. 2,930 responses from 293 respondents on 10 items.
Reference: Qi X, Xu HN (2024). The impact of nurses' stress situation coping on somatization: a mediated moderation model. PeerJ, 12, e18658. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.18658
Notes: `PSS0` in the deposited header is a typo for PSS4 -- it sits in position 4 of an otherwise complete PSS1..PSS10 -- and is renamed rather than dropped.

Description: Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support (MSPSS), 12 items on a 1-7 scale, Chinese nurses. 3,516 responses from 293 respondents on 12 items.
Reference: Qi X, Xu HN (2024). The impact of nurses' stress situation coping on somatization: a mediated moderation model. PeerJ, 12, e18658. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.18658
Notes: Named PSSS* in the deposit. Header spacing is irregular (`PSSS 2`) and is normalised.

Description: Coping Inventory for Stressful Situations (CISS), 21 items on a 1-5 scale, Chinese nurses. 6,153 responses from 293 respondents on 21 items.
Reference: Qi X, Xu HN (2024). The impact of nurses' stress situation coping on somatization: a mediated moderation model. PeerJ, 12, e18658. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.18658
Notes: One of five instruments in one deposited sheet.

Description: Acceptance and Action Questionnaire-II (AAQ-II), 7 items on a 1-7 scale, Spanish soccer referees. 1,092 responses from 156 respondents on 7 items.
Reference: Arbinaga F, Moreno San Pedro E, Mendoza-Sierra MI (2025). Psychopathological symptoms in soccer referees: the role of psychological inflexibility and perfectionism. PeerJ, 13, e19790. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.19790
Notes: One of three instruments in one deposited .sav. No respondent identifier in the deposit, so id is row position.

Description: Sport Anxiety Scale, 45 items on a 0-4 scale, Spanish soccer referees. 7,020 responses from 156 respondents on 45 items.
Reference: Arbinaga F, Moreno San Pedro E, Mendoza-Sierra MI (2025). Psychopathological symptoms in soccer referees: the role of psychological inflexibility and perfectionism. PeerJ, 13, e19790. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.19790
Notes: The deposit's SAF* columns are the authors' subscale totals, not responses, and are excluded.

Description: Multidimensional Perfectionism Scale, 31 items on a 1-5 scale, Spanish soccer referees. 4,836 responses from 156 respondents on 31 items.
Reference: Arbinaga F, Moreno San Pedro E, Mendoza-Sierra MI (2025). Psychopathological symptoms in soccer referees: the role of psychological inflexibility and perfectionism. PeerJ, 13, e19790. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.19790
Notes: The deposit numbers this block to 38 with gaps; only the 31 columns present are included, each keeping its source number so items stay matchable to the published instrument. MPS3 and MPS23 are observed 1-4 only -- category non-use in 156 referees, not a separate scale. MPSF* are the authors' subscale totals and are excluded.

Description: Simplified Coping Style Questionnaire (SCSQ), 20 items on a 0-3 scale, Chinese family caregivers of haematopoietic stem cell transplant patients. 4,000 responses from 200 respondents on 20 items.
Reference: Fan X, Zhang Y, Yan J, Kang Z, Wei Y, Guo X, Liu Y, Chen J, Ding D (2026). Social support and care burden in family caregivers of patients with hematologic malignancies: a parallel mediation model of coping strategies. PeerJ, 14, e21527. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.21527
Notes: Item names are the deposit's own descriptive English labels, which are the only item identifiers it carries.

Description: Caregiver Burden Inventory (CBI), 24 items on a 0-4 scale, Chinese family caregivers of haematopoietic stem cell transplant patients. 4,800 responses from 200 respondents on 24 items.
Reference: Fan X, Zhang Y, Yan J, Kang Z, Wei Y, Guo X, Liu Y, Chen J, Ding D (2026). Social support and care burden in family caregivers of patients with hematologic malignancies: a parallel mediation model of coping strategies. PeerJ, 14, e21527. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.21527
Notes: The deposit's third block, social_support_01..32, is deliberately NOT in IRW: it is the SSRS with its 10 questions expanded into one column per response option, mixing 1-4 ratings, 0/1 checkboxes and one constant column. The instrument is the Caregiver Burden Inventory (Novak & Guest, 1989), which the paper names and which has the 24 items and 0-4 scoring seen here; an earlier version of this row and of data/fan_2026_caregivers.py called it the Zarit Burden Interview, a different 22-item instrument.

Description: Microplastics awareness and concern, 3 binary items (heard of microplastics; concern for health; concern for the environment), Romanian respondents. 1,251 responses from 417 respondents on 3 items.
Reference: Pop V, Ozunu A, Petrescu DC, Stan AD, Petrescu-Mag RM (2023). The influence of media narratives on microplastics risk perception. PeerJ, 11, e16338. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.16338
Notes: Split from pop_2023_mp_media because the two blocks run on different response scales. Full English item wording is the deposit's column headers.

Description: Microplastics information known from the media, 8 items on a 1-7 scale, Romanian respondents. 3,336 responses from 417 respondents on 8 items.
Reference: Pop V, Ozunu A, Petrescu DC, Stan AD, Petrescu-Mag RM (2023). The influence of media narratives on microplastics risk perception. PeerJ, 11, e16338. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.16338
Notes: Questions 4-11 of the same survey as pop_2023_mp_concern; kept separate because that block is binary and this one is 1-7.

Description: Beliefs about Medicines Questionnaire (BMQ), 18 items on a 1-5 scale, Malaysian hypertensive outpatients. 2,880 responses from 160 respondents on 18 items.
Reference: Aziz F, Malek S, Mhd Ali A, Wong MS, Mosleh M, Milow P (2020). Determining hypertensive patients' beliefs towards medication and associations with medication adherence using machine learning methods. PeerJ, 8, e8286. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.8286
Notes: The sheet interleaves the authors' subscale totals (Specific Necessity, Specific Concern, General Overused, General Harm) with the items; those are excluded. The B block is not in numerical order in the file and is not renumbered, so items stay matchable to the published BMQ. No respondent identifier in the deposit, so id is row position.

Description: Medication adherence scale, 8 items on a 0-4 scale, Malaysian hypertensive outpatients. 1,280 responses from 160 respondents on 8 items.
Reference: Aziz F, Malek S, Mhd Ali A, Wong MS, Mosleh M, Milow P (2020). Determining hypertensive patients' beliefs towards medication and associations with medication adherence using machine learning methods. PeerJ, 8, e8286. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.8286
Notes: The `Adherence Level` column is the authors' composite and is excluded. No respondent identifier in the deposit, so id is row position.

Description: Malay Internet Addiction Test (M-IAT), 20 items on a 0-5 scale, Malaysian adolescents. 8,400 responses from 420 respondents on 20 items.
Reference: Md Bukhori AB, Ja'afar MH (2024). Internet addiction among adolescents during the COVID-19 pandemic: Associations with sociodemographic and psychological distress. PeerJ, 12, e17489. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.17489
Notes: The deposited SurveyMonkey export has a TWO-ROW header (block label above item wording); read as a single header row the items collapse into `Unnamed:` columns, which is why upstream triage saw no item structure. Items are numbered from the source's own numbering within each block. Total Score columns are composites and are excluded.

Description: Malay DASS-21, 21 items on a 0-3 scale, Malaysian adolescents. 8,820 responses from 420 respondents on 21 items.
Reference: Md Bukhori AB, Ja'afar MH (2024). Internet addiction among adolescents during the COVID-19 pandemic: Associations with sociodemographic and psychological distress. PeerJ, 12, e17489. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.17489
Notes: From the same two-row-header export as bukhori_2024_iat; see that table's note.

Description: Political knowledge battery, 6 binary items, US survey respondents. 16,815 responses from 2,807 respondents on 6 items.
Reference: Fitz EB, Stecuła DA, Hitt MP, Saunders KL (2024). Objective numeracy exacerbates framing effects from decision-making under political risk. Scientific reports, 14, 10473. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-61099-y
Notes: The article is CC BY; the data are deposited separately at Harvard Dataverse (doi:10.7910/DVN/MMOGJI) and were reached from the paper's Data Availability statement. These 6 items are already scored 0/1 in the deposit.

Description: Objective numeracy battery, 11 binary-scored items, US survey respondents; resp_raw carries the original free-text answer. 30,722 responses from 2,806 respondents on 11 items.
Reference: Fitz EB, Stecuła DA, Hitt MP, Saunders KL (2024). Objective numeracy exacerbates framing effects from decision-making under political risk. Scientific reports, 14, 10473. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-61099-y
Notes: Nine of the eleven items are free text in the deposit ('50%', 'half the time', 'about 500'). Scoring is not a judgment made here: the authors' replication .do file enumerates every string they counted as correct, and the processing script parses that file at run time and applies it. numeracy4 and numeracy5 are multiple choice and the .do recodes them by option number (3 and 2 correct). One deliberate difference from the authors' Stata: their recode scores a BLANK as incorrect; a blank is a non-response, so blanks are dropped here instead (14-33 per item out of 2,813). Data DOI 10.7910/DVN/MMOGJI.

Description: Joint Simon task, capuchin monkeys, trial-level accuracy. Items are the stimulus probe (experimental condition crossed with trial type, 16 in all); compatibility travels as an item covariate because trial type determines it exactly. resp is the experiment program's own correctness scoring. 2,753 responses from 10 subjects on 16 items.
Reference: Martínez M, Babb MH, Range F, Brosnan SF (2024). The Joint Simon task is not joint for capuchin monkeys. Scientific Reports, 14, 5937. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-55885-x
Notes: Below the 100-id floor in datastandard.md; accepted on ben-domingue's ruling of 2026-09-16 (irw#2220), that the floor is a survey-shaped proxy and a trials-based design inverts the shape. Non-human respondents: tag accordingly (irw#2206). Trials where the monkey did not respond carry a third code (2) in the source's scoring column and are dropped rather than scored 0 -- 49 here. The deposit's correct_rv string column labels those inconsistently (9 of 49 as 'correct') and is not used. Monkey names are lowercased because the two sheets disagree on case.

Description: Go/no-go control task from the same capuchin study, trial-level accuracy, 8 stimulus probes (reward/no-reward crossed with trial type). 712 responses from 10 subjects on 8 items.
Reference: Martínez M, Babb MH, Range F, Brosnan SF (2024). The Joint Simon task is not joint for capuchin monkeys. Scientific Reports, 14, 5937. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-55885-x
Notes: Below the 100-id floor in datastandard.md; accepted on ben-domingue's ruling of 2026-09-16 (irw#2220), that the floor is a survey-shaped proxy and a trials-based design inverts the shape. Non-human respondents: tag accordingly (irw#2206). 88 no-response trials dropped; see martinez_2024_joint_simon for the scoring note.

Description: Detour task measuring inhibitory control in 8 bearded dragons and 24 tortoises. Items are the 20 trials in order (4 days x 5 trials), complete for every animal; read them as a learning sequence rather than as distinct probes. resp is 1 when the animal detoured successfully. 640 responses from 32 subjects on 20 items.
Reference: Santacà M, Wilkinson A, Stancher G, Sovrano VA, Bisazza A (2025). Lizards and tortoises show evidence of low inhibitory control. Scientific Reports, 15, 23446. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-08373-9
Notes: Below the 100-id floor in datastandard.md; accepted on ben-domingue's ruling of 2026-09-16 (irw#2220), that the floor is a survey-shaped proxy and a trials-based design inverts the shape. Non-human respondents: tag accordingly (irw#2206). id is the species prefixed onto the source Subject, because the dragons are named and the tortoises numbered. The deposit's Time_log is not emitted as rt: the standard requires seconds and the log's base is unstated (log10 gives 3-256s, natural log 1.6-11.1s, both plausible).

Description: Spontaneous-alternation T-maze, 21 adult rats, five sessions of 20 trials. resp is WHICH ARM the rat entered (1 = right, 0 = left), NOT whether it was correct: no arm is correct in this task and the construct the authors measure, alternation, is a property of consecutive trials. Do not model resp as accuracy. 1,077 responses from 21 subjects on 100 items.
Reference: Acevedo-Triana CA, Rojas MJ, Cardenas FP (2017). Running wheel training does not change neurogenesis levels or alter working memory tasks in adult rats. PeerJ, 5, e2976. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.2976
Notes: Below the 100-id floor in datastandard.md; accepted on ben-domingue's ruling of 2026-09-16 (irw#2220), that the floor is a survey-shaped proxy and a trials-based design inverts the shape. Non-human respondents: tag accordingly (irw#2206). The sheet's summary rows (Animals == 'TOTAL') are dropped, as are the Hab* habituation phases, which have no trials. Only 1,077 of 2,100 trials have an arm entry recorded; the other 1,022 have Right and Left both 0 (no entry within the time limit) and are dropped as non-responses, plus one row with both set to 1, which cannot be a single choice. The deposit's Alternation column is a per-session total on the summary rows, not a trial-level response, and is not used.

Description: AI models as respondents: 124 large language models (id = model name, verbatim, aliases not merged) scored on the 541 prompts of IFEval, an instruction-following benchmark whose prompts each carry 1-3 programmatically verifiable instructions (e.g. no commas, at least 300 words). resp is the number of the prompt's instructions the model's response satisfied under IFEval's strict check (0 to itemcov_n_instructions); resp == itemcov_n_instructions is prompt-level strict accuracy. From the OpenEval archive (Hugging Face Open-Eval-Commons/OpenEval, revision 23a1ded9), one run, scores only. Respondents are not independent: many models share base weights, decoding temperature varies across models (cov_temperature), and items may appear in training data.
Reference: Jiang, H., Zhang, S., Zhu, D., Bai, Y., Truong, S. T., Yi, X., Koyejo, S., Xie, X., & Xiao, Z. (2026). AI Evaluation Should Require Standardized Item-Level Data Releases. arXiv:2604.03244 (v2). Benchmark: Zhou, J., et al. (2023). Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models. arXiv:2311.07911.
Notes: CC BY-NC 4.0 is authoritative per the OpenEval authors (email to Ben Domingue, 2026-09-16), who granted inclusion of the model x item score tables with credit to the repository and paper; the HF card says the same, the GitHub repo carries no licence. NC inclusion approved by Ben 2026-09-19 (irw#2166). Scores only: no item text or model output, since the grant does not cover benchmark content. Permission on file at licenseinfo/emails/openeval_jiang_2026.md.

Description: Behavioral Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (BERQ), Peruvian Spanish adaptation, 20 items in five four-item subscales (seeking distraction, withdrawal, actively approaching, seeking social support, ignoring), 403 adults aged 18-59 in Lima. 8,060 responses. The paper documents a 5-point scale from 1 (seldom) to 5 (almost always); the deposit stores it zero-indexed, so resp is 0-4 and shipped as recorded rather than shifted. No missing data: the authors report the online form required completion and that no imputation was applied.
Reference: López-Odar, D., Aguirre-Morales, M., Cirilo-Acero, I., Hervias-Guerra, E., Vara-Horna, A., & Deza-Villanueva, S. (2025). Psychometric Properties of the Behavioral–Emotional Regulation Questionnaire in Peruvian Adults (BERQ-PA). Behavioral Sciences, 15(2), 224. https://doi.org/10.3390/bs15020224
Notes: The ERQ block in the same deposit is NOT in IRW: the paper documents the Peruvian ERQ as 7-point (1-7) and the deposited ERQ1-ERQ10 hold five levels 0-4 across all 403 respondents, so the responses cannot be mapped to the documented anchors. Held pending an author query. Item text not shipped -- BERQ is a third-party instrument (Kraaij & Garnefski 2019; Spanish adaptation Dominguez-Lara et al. 2022) and the deposit is a plain CSV with positional column names and no labels of any kind.

Description: General Health Questionnaire GHQ-28 (Goldberg & Hillier 1979), 28 items in four seven-item dimensions (somatic symptoms, anxiety, social dysfunction, depression), administered to the same 403 Peruvian adults as lopezodar_2025_berq. 11,284 responses on the documented 4-point scale, 0 (not at all) to 3 (much more than usual).
Reference: López-Odar, D., Aguirre-Morales, M., Cirilo-Acero, I., Hervias-Guerra, E., Vara-Horna, A., & Deza-Villanueva, S. (2025). Psychometric Properties of the Behavioral–Emotional Regulation Questionnaire in Peruvian Adults (BERQ-PA). Behavioral Sciences, 15(2), 224. https://doi.org/10.3390/bs15020224
Notes: Two QC warnings, both checked and expected in a community sample: GHQ1 ('feeling perfectly well and in good health') has 67% of responses at one value, and GHQ28, the item about wishing you were dead, is observed 0-2 because the top category is unendorsed -- category non-use, not a different permitted set. The authors report no missing data and no imputation. Item text not shipped: third-party instrument, positional column names, plain CSV with no label level.

Description: ICF-RS-17, a 17-item functional assessment tool built from the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health via a three-round Delphi study, then validated on 2,574 inpatients at 12 Chinese rehabilitation institutions (Nanjing, Wuxi, Suzhou, Aug 2021-Mar 2023). Each patient was rated on all 17 ICF categories at admission and again at discharge, so wave 1 = admission and wave 2 = discharge; 87,516 responses. resp is the 0-10 Numerical Rating Scale the paper defines, where 0 = no problem and 10 = complete problem -- HIGHER IS WORSE functioning. item is the ICF category code as the source spells it (d450, b455, ...).
Reference: Li, J., Xu, G., Jin, J., Li, N., Li, J., & Liu, S. (2025). Development and validation of a functional assessment tool for Chinese inpatient rehabilitation: insights from a Delphi study based on the International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health (ICF). PeerJ, 13, e20280. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.20280
Notes: 35 rows (16 profiles) in the source file are exact duplicates across all 37 columns; two patients matching on all 34 ratings of an 0-10 scale is not a coincidence and the profiles are not degenerate. They are KEPT rather than dropped: the file has no id column, the paper's own N is 2,574, and removing them would publish a different sample than the article analyses. Users who need de-duplicated data can drop ids whose full response profile is identical. The b/d item prefixes are ICF's own chapter codes (body functions / activities and participation), not two instruments -- the paper validates ICF-RS-17 as a single two-factor tool, so do not split it. Item text not yet shipped: the 17 ICF category names are in the paper's Tables 3-4 (paper_explicit, needs a Step 5b verification), not in the data file.

Description: Relationship Assessment Scale (RAS; Hendrick 1988), Polish translation by Monfort et al. (2014), 7 items on a 1-5 scale, merged across the paper's three independently recruited samples: the reference sample (733) and validation samples 1 (203) and 2 (209), distinguished by cov_study. 1,145 respondents, 8,015 responses. id is prefixed with the sample because the samples were recruited independently.
Reference: Adamczyk, K., Kleka, P., & Frydrychowicz, M. (2022). Psychometric functioning, measurement invariance, and external associations of the Relationship Assessment Scale in a sample of Polish adults. Scientific Reports, 12, 22077. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-022-26653-6
Notes: IMPORTANT -- items 4 and 7 are harmonised. The three samples do not agree on how the two negatively worded items are stored: validation sample 1 deposits them raw (RAS4 mean 1.88) alongside explicit reverse-scored copies (RAS4_R mean 4.12, r = -1.0), while the reference sample and validation sample 2 deposit only the reverse-scored direction (means 4.24 and 4.15). This table uses the reverse-scored column for validation sample 1, so all three samples run the same direction for every item -- after harmonisation RAS4 reads 4.24/4.12/4.15 and RAS7 reads 3.65/3.59/3.49 across the samples. Nothing was recomputed: the reversed columns are the depositors' own. Consequence for item text: for items 4 and 7 the shipped resp runs OPPOSITE to the A-E anchors printed in the deposit's materials document. From the OSF deposit's SPSS files. No variable labels and no value labels on any item column in any of the three files -- both levels checked -- so item text has no data_labels route; the deposit's materials document prints the Polish wording for several of these instruments and is the source a later itemtext pass should use.

Description: Occupational Sitting and Physical Activity Questionnaire (OSPAQ), 4 items asking the percentage of work time spent sitting, standing, walking and on heavy physical tasks; 385 Belgian office workers.
Reference: Maes I, Ketels M, Van Dyck D, Clays E. 2020. The occupational sitting and physical activity questionnaire (OSPAQ): a validation study with accelerometer-assessed measures in Belgian office workers. BMC Public Health 20:1072.
Notes: resp is a percentage (continuous 0-100), not an ordinal category. The four items are a time allocation and are meant to total 100; for 28 respondents they do not, and those responses ship exactly as deposited rather than being rescaled. 999 is a sentinel missing code (3 cells) and is dropped, not shipped. The accelerometer columns are device measurements of the same four postures and ship as covariates, never as items. Item text not shipped: the headers are posture labels, not the administered stems.

Description: Eight-task cognitive battery (physical, social and inhibitory-control domains) administered to 138 Japanese macaques; resp is per-trial binary success, 6,356 trials.
Reference: Kaigaishi Y, Yamamoto S. 2024. Higher eigenvector centrality in grooming network is linked to better inhibitory control task performance but not other cognitive tasks in Japanese macaques. Scientific Reports 14:27460.
Notes: Subjects are Japanese macaques; id is the focal unit measured, per the data standard. One table rather than three because the workbook's physical/social/inhibition sheets are domains of a single battery given to one colony, kept as itemcov_domain; split apart, none clears the 100-subject floor. The deposit's own `trial` counter does NOT uniquely index a trial (36 subject-task-trial triples repeat, 20 with an identical timestamp), so trial_number is a sequential index within subject and task in the file's row order and the source counter is retained as trial_source. The ~25 social-network statistics per row are the paper's derived predictors, not subject attributes, and are not shipped. Item text not applicable: the items are tasks, not worded questions.

Notes: Items q16, q22, q23 (paper: Cronbach alpha 0.80); the paper dichotomises them, the table keeps the raw 0-6 codes. Covariates are the deposit's raw codes per its Coding manual.docx: cov_gender_identity (0 male, 1 female, 2 transgender woman, 3 transgender man, 4 other), cov_sexual_orientation (0-6), cov_relationship_status (0-5), cov_hiv_status (0-3), cov_knows_where_to_test (0/1), cov_preferred_test_method (0 hospital ... 4 self-testing; the paper's outcome), cov_last_hiv_test (0-5), cov_age (years), cov_education (0-8), cov_employment (0-12), cov_income (0-6, 6 = declined). date = date of participation (Unix seconds). Same id = same person across sison_2022_hiv_testing_stigma and sison_2022_provider_mistrust.

Description: Provider mistrust at HIV testing facilities (4 author-constructed items) on a 0-6 agreement scale, Filipino men who have sex with men and transgender women recruited online and in Metro Manila venues (2016). 3,596 responses from 899 respondents on 4 items.

Association of anticipated HIV testing stigma and provider mistrust on preference for HIV self-testing among cisgender men who have sex with men in the Philippines. BMC Public Health, 22, 2362. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-022-14834-x
Notes: Items q18-q21 (paper: Cronbach alpha 0.89); the paper dichotomises them, the table keeps the raw 0-6 codes. Covariates are the deposit's raw codes per its Coding manual.docx: cov_gender_identity (0 male, 1 female, 2 transgender woman, 3 transgender man, 4 other), cov_sexual_orientation (0-6), cov_relationship_status (0-5), cov_hiv_status (0-3), cov_knows_where_to_test (0/1), cov_preferred_test_method (0 hospital ... 4 self-testing; the paper's outcome), cov_last_hiv_test (0-5), cov_age (years), cov_education (0-8), cov_employment (0-12), cov_income (0-6, 6 = declined). date = date of participation (Unix seconds). All 899 respondents ship; the paper analyses the 803 cisgender MSM (cov_gender_identity 0, excluding heterosexual men). Authors' dichotomised recodes excluded. Same id = same person across sison_2022_hiv_testing_stigma and sison_2022_provider_mistrust.

Description: Chinese Male Smoking Rationalisation Scale (Huang et al., 2020), 26 items in six subscales on a 1-5 agreement scale, adult male smokers in Guiyang, China. 16,016 responses from 616 respondents on 26 items.
Reference: Zhang D, Chen WJ, Meng XX, Zhao X, Liu RH, Tian HY (2024). Breaking down barriers: rationalisations and motivation to stop among Chinese male smokers under cigarette dependence. BMC Public Health, 24, 1812. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-024-19295-y
Notes: Item codes keep the subscale prefixes: SFB1-5 smoking functional, RGB1-3 risk generalisation, SAB1-6 social acceptability, SSB1-4 safe smoking, SEB1-5 self-exempting, QHB1-3 quitting-is-harmful beliefs. Raw agreement direction (5 = strongly agree), not the paper's reversed IPMA coding. Covariates are raw SPSS codes: cov_mtss (Motivation To Stop Scale, a single 1-7 item), cov_age_group (2 = 18-24 ... 7 = 65+), cov_education (1-5), cov_residence (1 city, 2 township), cov_occupation (1-6), cov_age_first_smoked (banded, 1 = below 11 ... 8 = 65+). All respondents are adult male current smokers (street-intercept survey, Guiyang, Nov-Dec 2023); the deposit is the authors' analytic sample of 616 after removing straight-liners. id is the questionnaire number; same id = same person across zhang_2024_smoking_rationalisation and zhang_2024_ftcd.

Description: Fagerstrom Test for Cigarette Dependence (FTCD/FTND), 6 items scored 0-3 (ND1, ND4) or 0-1 (others), adult male smokers in Guiyang, China. 3,696 responses from 616 respondents on 6 items.
Reference: Zhang D, Chen WJ, Meng XX, Zhao X, Liu RH, Tian HY (2024). Breaking down barriers: rationalisations and motivation to stop among Chinese male smokers under cigarette dependence. BMC Public Health, 24, 1812. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-024-19295-y
Notes: Items ND1-ND6 as standard FTND scoring points (mixed 0-3/0-1 widths are the instrument's design). The deposit's FTND and HSI sum scores excluded. Covariates are raw SPSS codes: cov_mtss (Motivation To Stop Scale, a single 1-7 item), cov_age_group (2 = 18-24 ... 7 = 65+), cov_education (1-5), cov_residence (1 city, 2 township), cov_occupation (1-6), cov_age_first_smoked (banded, 1 = below 11 ... 8 = 65+). Description: Pregnancy Vaccine Hesitancy Scale, Malay version (pVHS-M), 10-item validation form on a 1-5 agreement scale (1 strongly disagree, 5 strongly agree), COVID-19 vaccine attitudes of pregnant women attending an obstetrics clinic in Kelantan, Malaysia. 2,000 responses from 200 respondents on 10 items.
Reference: Che Mood NA, Mat Yudin Z, Ahmad WMAW, Abdul Kadir A, Mohd Noor N, Md Nawawi NH, Mohamad Zon E, Ali N (2024). Validation of the questionnaire "Pregnancy Vaccine Hesitancy Scale (pVHS)" toward COVID-19 vaccine for Malaysian pregnant women. PeerJ, 12, e17134. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.17134
Notes: All 10 administered items ship, including pL5 and pL9, which the paper's EFA dropped from the final 8-item scale. pL5 and pL9 (side-effect worries) are stored UNREVERSED: the paper reflects them for analysis, and its 10-item alpha of 0.859 is reproduced only after reflecting them (0.887 as stored). Higher resp = more agreement with the item as worded. No respondent identifier or covariates in the deposit; id is row position.

Description: Knowledge about exercise (Part 2 of the KAP exercise and exergames questionnaire), 9 statements rated agree/neutral/disagree (1 disagree, 2 neutral, 3 agree), Malaysian urban high school students aged 13-17. 1,674 responses from 186 respondents on 9 items.
Reference: Abdulkader Mohamed R, Abdul Rahim NA, Mohamad SM, Ahmad Yusof H (2022). Validity and reliability of knowledge, attitude, and practice regarding exercise and exergames experiences questionnaire among high school students. BMC Public Health, 22, 1743. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-022-14147-z
Notes: resp is agreement with the statement, not correctness: some statements are false (e.g. 'Exercise does more harm than good'), so direction differs across items. Split by the administered block and its response format (knowledge 3-point, attitude 5-point, exergames yes/no); the paper's post-hoc EFA (Table 4) later moved items between the knowledge and attitude domains and dropped four, so these tables are the administered blocks with every administered item, not the paper's final domains. Item codes are positional (know_/att_/exg_ in workbook column order); the header->code map is printed by the script. No respondent identifier or demographics in the deposit, so id is row position and the same id is the same student across abdulkader_mohamed_2022_exer_knowledge, _exer_attitude and _exergame_exp. Two rows that were exact 33-column copies of earlier rows (double submissions) were dropped: 188 -> 186 respondents. The practice block (yes/no screeners with days/week and minutes/day counts) is not shipped.
